limitations: Monitor jobs are FIFO, identical-cost, and nonpreemptive. Production queries can have variable cost, priority, cancellation, or coalescing.
Worker service is expressed in request-equivalent time and assumes a stationary arrival-rate conversion.
The model processes every declared look. Dropping superseded checks can reduce queueing but changes the operational policy and requires a separate validity audit.
Unlimited workers are a lower-bound concurrency model; E76 synchronous blocking is the upper bound.
All earlier independence, traffic-weighting, delayed-label, and preregistration limitations remain.
model: Replay every declared checkpoint through asynchronous FIFO monitor worker pools. Each look is one job with fixed request-equivalent service time; alert action occurs when the first statistically crossing look finishes processing. Compare one, two, four, eight, and unlimited workers against E76's synchronous blocking upper bound.

validation.synchronous_bound: Every asynchronous worker-pool action cost is no greater than E76's synchronous blocking cost.
validation.unlimited_workers: Unlimited workers add exactly one service cost to the request-only per-case action oracle.
validation.worker_monotonicity: Median action delay is nondecreasing as worker count falls.
validation.zero_service_reproduction: Every worker policy reproduces E75 robust unique winner counts.
